name: AUTO_INCREMENT Alter
description: Alter the AUTO_INCREMENT value of MySQL database tables, via an admin UI, a service and Drush commands.
project_description: This module allows altering the AUTO_INCREMENT value of database tables. One common use case is to prevent entity ID conflicts when performing Drupal upgrades (see the core known-issues documentation on ID conflicts). At the moment the module only works with the MySQL driver, so the core drupal:mysql module must be enabled. It provides an admin interface at /admin/config/development/auto-increment-alter (added in alpha5), an auto_increment_alter.mysql service implementing AutoIncrementAlterInterface, and a set of Drush commands (auto-increment-alter:table, :tables, :content-entity, :content-entities, :value, :values, :table-list, :entity-list). Single-table and single-content-entity operations take a table/entity name and an integer value; bulk operations read the $settings['auto_increment_alter_tables'] and $settings['auto_increment_alter_content_entities'] arrays from settings.php. Content-entity operations resolve base and revision tables through the entity_type.manager service. All admin routes are gated by the 'administer auto_increment table values' permission (restrict access: true).
